lines.text: Ohio and Michigan once nearly went to war... over Toledo.

parts.tts: Ohio and Michigan once nearly went to war...

lines.text: Blame a bad map. Both claimed one strip of land, 5 to 8 miles wide.

parts.tts: Blame a bad map. Both claimed one strip of land, five to eight miles wide.
parts.heard: blame a bad map. Both claimed one strip of land five to eight miles wide.

lines.text: In 1835, both sent militias to the Maumee River... and traded taunts.

parts.tts: In eighteen thirty-five, both sent militias to the Maumee River...

lines.text: The one battle? Reportedly, shots fired into the air. Nobody was hit.

lines.text: But here's the part... the war's only injury: a deputy, hurt with a penknife.

lines.text: By a man named Two Stickney. His brother? Reportedly named One.

lines.text: Congress stepped in. Ohio got Toledo. Michigan got statehood... and the Upper Peninsula.

lines.text: A consolation prize almost everyone called a worthless wilderness.

lines.text: But in the eighteen-forties, they found copper and iron. By the eighteen-sixties, it supplied 90 percent of America's copper.
